clue.text: Advocate parking by a stretch of river

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for parking, as on road signs
a reach is a straight length of river between bends

explanation.surface: Someone argues for a car park beside a stretch of river.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate a cause is to urge it publicly, as a preacher urges a sermon's message.

clue.text: Eliminate introduction about beginning of chapter

indicators.note: about means the first word's letters go round the next piece

parts.note: a prelude is an introductory piece or event

indicators.note: beginning of means only the opening letter of chapter is used

explanation.surface: An editor cuts a preface that wraps round the start of a chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: To preclude something is to rule it out in advance, removing the possibility.

clue.text: Pity a clue has to be rewritten "Sources of oil"

indicators.note: to be rewritten says the letters of the words before are written out again in a new order

explanation.surface: A setter regrets that a clue about oil sources must be redone.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucalyptus trees yield the aromatic oil used in remedies and inhalants.

clue.text: Boasted a band

explanation.surface: Someone bragged about a music group.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to boast, with an old past tense form; a team of workers or sailors is also this group.

clue.text: Opera chap, not English, possibly to make overtures

indicators.note: possibly says the remaining letters may be arranged another way
not says the letter for English is taken out of the word opera

explanation.surface: A man at the opera, minus his Englishness, perhaps tries to start talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes E from OPERA, leaving OPRA; 'possibly' then rearranges OPRA with CHAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Making overtures means sounding someone out with a first proposal, which is what one does on going up to them.

clue.text: See 9
Thorough when measuring the depth again

explanation.surface: A complete job, done by sounding the depth a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits into RE (again) and SOUNDING, the sailor's word for measuring water depth with a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A resounding victory is a complete, emphatic one; sounding water is gauging its depth, so doing it once more fits the second sense.

clue.text: A second city" affair

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city that crosswords use constantly

explanation.surface: A second city's romantic liaison.
explanation.definitionFit: A French word used in English for a love affair, especially a secret one.

clue.text: Mineral contributing to a lethal item

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mineral plays its part in some deadly object.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock salt is the mineral form of sodium chloride, mined as a crystal.

clue.text: Tense but rosy outlook?

explanation.surface: A nervous person nonetheless sees good times ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading turns the phrase round: a perfect future is a rosy outlook. 'Tense' looks like an adjective for nerves but is the grammar term.
explanation.definitionFit: The grammatical form 'will have done' is this tense; a flawless time ahead is an optimistic prospect.

clue.text: Former scrutineer, we hear, in state department

indicators.note: we hear says the words before are judged by their sound when spoken

parts.note: ex means former, and a checker is someone who scrutinises

explanation.surface: An ex-inspector is reportedly working in a government department.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exchequer is the UK government office that manages public revenue, a department of state.

clue.text: Gloomy expression as boat left

parts.note: a scow is a flat-bottomed boat

explanation.surface: Someone looks glum watching a boat leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A frown of displeasure or anger is a dark look on the face.

clue.text: In halting way, the member leaves a flower

indicators.note: leaves says the member's letters depart from the longer word

parts.note: walking haltingly is walking limply
MP is short for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A limping member of the group exits, leaving a flower behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like foliage beside 'a flower', but it is the verb: MP leaves LIMPLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A white trumpet-shaped bloom grown from a bulb, often used at funerals and Easter.

clue.text: Sailor returns to desk career, initially as an official

parts.note: a bureau is a writing desk

indicators.note: initially says take only the opening letter of career
returns says the sailor's word is read back to front

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor comes back to an office job, becoming a civil servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A government functionary following procedures is a classic administrative official.

clue.text: Incorrectly placed loci (but only a small fault)

indicators.note: incorrectly says the following letters are not in their proper order

explanation.surface: Putting the loci in the wrong place is only a minor slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor sin or trifling offence, from the Spanish for a little sin.

clue.text: Drain the river containing muddy pelt

indicators.note: containing says the river's letters hold the next piece inside

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain, a favourite crossword river

indicators.note: muddy means confused, so the letters of pelt are mixed up

explanation.surface: A river carries off a muddy animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhaust or use up a supply is to empty it out.

clue.text: Unusual diet Greek character turns to in boredom

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of diet appear in an odd order
turns says the Greek letter's name is reversed

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A strange diet turns a Greek into a bored person.
explanation.definitionFit: Weariness from something dull and repetitive is the state of being bored.

clue.text: An unsound hint with a clue would be improper

indicators.note: unsound says the letters are not in a sound order

explanation.surface: Giving a hint along with a clue would be cheating.
explanation.definitionFit: Something morally wrong or against professional rules is improper conduct.

clue.text: I change position regularly in the works?

definitions.text: I change position regularly in the works?

parts.words: I change position regularly in the works?
parts.note: the works are a clock's mechanism, where a weight swings to and fro at a steady rate

explanation.surface: A factory worker who keeps moving between stations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' suggests a factory, but here it is the inside of a clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A swinging weight that regulates a clock moves back and forth at fixed intervals.

clue.text: I'm for cutting certain food supplies

definitions.text: I'm for cutting certain food supplies

parts.words: I'm for cutting certain food supplies
parts.note: a kitchen device speaks, saying its job is to chop meat into fine pieces

explanation.surface: A politician declares support for food budget cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting supplies' reads as reducing rations; the speaker is a kitchen machine that literally cuts food.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that chops meat finely is the speaker of the clue.

clue.text: The meal for members of the race?

definitions.text: The meal for members of the race?

parts.words: The meal for members of the race?
parts.note: a self-service spread where guests help themselves is pictured as food for those taking part in a race

explanation.surface: A question about what athletes in a race eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for a meal served for people standing and moving about is read literally as a spread for runners.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-up self-service meal where guests circulate is called this, and runners in a race would literally eat at one.

clue.text: Man's religion (eastern) supplying aromatic liquid

parts.note: Ben is a man's name
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A man's Eastern faith provides a fragrant liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: The simplest aromatic hydrocarbon, a colourless liquid, gave its name to the whole aromatic class of compounds.

clue.text: See 20
End protest

explanation.surface: Stop the demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim or purpose is an end; to raise an objection is to protest.

clue.text: This could be used for cutting tin

definitions.text: This could be used for cutting tin

parts.words: This could be used for cutting tin
parts.note: a tin is a loaf baked in a rectangular tin, so the cutting tool is a kitchen blade for loaves

explanation.surface: A metalworker's tool for cutting sheet tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tin' suggests metal, but a tin loaf is a common British bread shape baked in a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A serrated kitchen blade is used for slicing loaves, including the tin loaf.

clue.text: A time to muse

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A good moment to sit and think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muse' looks like the verb 'ponder', but it is the noun: one of the nine Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she is the Muse of love poetry, one of the nine daughters of Zeus.

clue.text: What one can do with light storage place

definitions.text: What one can do with light

explanation.surface: Casting light and keeping things in a garden hut.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast or give off light is a verb sense; a garden hut for tools is the noun.

clue.text: Stake erected in Sicily

indicators.note: erected in a down clue means the word is built upwards, so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: an ante is a poker stake put up before the deal

explanation.surface: A post set up on the island of Sicily.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is the volcano found in Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe's highest active volcano stands on the east coast of the Italian island.

clue.text: A mile trip to deliver the message

indicators.note: trip suggests stumbling, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Walking a mile to hand over a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending a note electronically is a modern way to get word to someone.

clue.text: Lied in act being worked, all the same

indicators.note: being worked means the letters are being kneaded into a new shape

explanation.surface: Lying while an act is being performed makes no difference.
explanation.definitionFit: Things exactly alike, with no difference between them, are all the same.

clue.text: Complete, yet only approximate

parts.note: tho is an informal short spelling of though, meaning yet
a rough figure is an approximate one

explanation.surface: Finished, though only approximately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only' is a link here; THO is the clipped spelling of 'though'.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete or exhaustive job leaves nothing out.

clue.text: The French in wrong city district

indicators.note: in says the French article sits inside the other word

parts.note: to wrong someone is to harm them
le is French for the

explanation.surface: French people treated badly in part of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A neighbourhood in northern Manhattan, New York, famous for its jazz-age renaissance.
